#4153. Caleb's third Myth has finally arrived in Love and Deepspace, and it's good news for all the husbandbro fans out there

Love and Deepspace has kicked off a new event, squarely built around Caleb's new Memory Pair.

Love and Deepspace’s latest update is here, adding a new Memory Pair for Caleb. The event is dubbed Ghosts' Final March, and it’s available now as part of a new Limited Wish Pool, as it has always worked.

The new Memory Pair is a 5-Star Solar-Slot, which can be obtained through the aforementioned Wish Pool. Doing so will unlock the Netherlord Companion for Caleb, and there’s even more for you to explore in this one.

Alongside the big new Memory Pair, Ghosts' Final March also offers the opportunity to earn a new 4-Star Solar-Slot Memory Pair, alongside ten Deepspace Wishes, 500 Diamonds, and other freebies. The event ends on April 11, so you have some time to get in and play.

If you’re only interested in the 5-Star variants, you’ll be happy to know that Infold is sticking with 150 pulls as the absolute maximum to guarantee earning Netherlord. This will be automatically unlocked after you pull both Nether Yearning and Nether Parting through the Wish Pool.

Obtaining either of the two will give you access to all chapters for the new Myth that’s also available as part of this event: Yin Yang Sundering. You can read all the lore once either of the two Memories have been unlocked, and you won’t even need to upgrade either of them.

The Lost Souls event has also kicked off alongside the new update. You can take part to claim a 4-Star Solar Slor Memory Pair for Caleb: Duskshard Dreams and Duskshard Lotus. You can also earn the 3-Star Memory, Lotus Bond, alongside some other freebies like more Wishes, Diamonds, Photo Poses, and an event-exclusive title.

After you unlock Caleb’s Netherlord Companion, you may want to fight alongside him to get another 4-Star Memory for free. You’ll need to challenge the the Rehearsal Stage to do so, and your first clear is guaranteed to get you the Duskshard Lotus Memory.

If you’re new to Love and Deepspace, or you simply want a refresher, we’ve put together a guide to help you wrap your head around Myths; how they work and how to unlock them. Banners are also an important part of any gacha game, Love and Deepspace included, so here’s how banners work, and what the current and next banners are.

#4152. South Of Midnight Director Reflects On Why He Was 'Always Worried' About Funding At Xbox

"It just seems like, in hindsight at least, it was unsustainable."

We absolutely loved South of Midnight when it launched last year as an Xbox first-party title from Compulsion Games, and it's still one of our favourite Xbox Game Studios releases of recent years. However, a year later, Xbox has parted ways with the development team and helped transition them back to an independent studio.

In a nutshell, it seems Xbox wasn't happy enough with South of Midnight's performance from a revenue standpoint, and the same could be said for other smaller releases last year like Double Fine's Keeper and Kiln.

Some fans had been voicing their concerns prior to these releases that Xbox might be putting too much funding into them, and speaking on a recent podcast, South of Midnight director David Sears admitted that he was "always worried" that the funding situation might change and cause Xbox to "close the floodgates".

Here's an excerpt from the MinnMax podcast in which he said this:

"I mean, [Xbox] were funding a lot of games. They were also funding a lot of studios that, you know, I was like, well, okay, great. I guess you have infinite money. Like I was saying earlier, I don't want to feel the weight of the obligation of giant budget or an army of 600 to be responsible for. I want to make something that isn't going to bankrupt Microsoft, I guess, or the games division."

"So, you know, on one hand, if everyone you're working with is either trying to make generational games at not a huge expense, or games that have huge or really significant contemporary commercial appeal, great. It's going to work. But when does that ever happen?"

"I literally told people, 'Wow, this could be terrible.' Because somebody is going to say one day, 'We're closing those floodgates.' And that's going to have really traumatic results downstream."

Perhaps most shockingly, the director went on to admit that as much as he wanted to make South of Midnight, it perhaps wasn't sustainable from a funding perspective in hindsight, and that a "shocking outcome" seemed inevitable.

"I mean, I wanted to make it. No doubt, and obviously, because we made it. Would I have turned off someone else's money flow before South of Midnight? Yeah, 'cause I'm not completely selfless. But it just seems like, in hindsight at least, it was unsustainable. So, of course it was going to have a shocking outcome."

"I mean, it's easy to dissect it now. At the time, I would talk to other directors and would be like, 'How is this happening? How did we get so lucky? Is this a golden era?' And I would always be like, 'For now, right? There's always a night when Rome burns.' And I didn't know exactly when it would be, but I was always worried about it."

Of course, none of this is to suggest that Sears wasn't proud of South of Midnight, or that he didn't think it was worthwhile, but it just appears he was concerned with the Xbox money was putting into (and expecting back) for it.

Nevertheless, it seems like he had a very positive experience working with Microsoft overall:

"To their credit, it's amazing, right? I think there's definitely corporate Microsoft DNA but they're vastly different from the Microsoft I knew back in the '90s or the early 2000s, right? Much more humane, actually. It's remarkable and commendable."

"Working on South of Midnight, it became clear to me - some games, their time is not on release. Some games are generational, right? Something that has a good message or is transportive to places that will remain timeless will endure and audiences will find them."

His prediction did ultimately come true - Xbox decided to "close the floodgates" earlier this year by splitting from multiple studios including Compulsion Games, and seemingly adopting a new strategy of focusing on their core franchises like Halo, Forza, Gears, Fallout and others.

We're just pleased that Compulsion Games didn't end up getting closed altogether, and that South of Midnight did actually see the light of day instead of being cancelled during development. We reckon it could end up being one of those Sunset Overdrive-style titles in the future - a cult classic that people end up really enjoying from years past.

#4151. The Petit Planet beta is coming back with new updates, but you still need to hope for an invite

If you've been missing Petit Planet since it was last available to play, you'll be happy to know that HoYoverse is hosting another test soon.

It’s been quite a while since we’ve heard anything about Petit Planet, the upcoming game from Genshin Impact and Honkai: Star Rail developer HoYoverse. By most accounts, Petit Planet is the studio’s take on Animal Crossing, though with a few interesting ideas of its own.

The game’s most recent test took place all the way back in November, but its next big test isn’t far off.

HoYoverse announced today that Petit Planet’s Stardrift Test is scheduled for April 21. This latest build will be available on PC, Android, and iOS. The beta will include new Neighbors, an updated Starsea Voyage, and more for you to do at the Galactic Bazaar.

Seeing as interacting with Neighbors is a core part of this life sim RPG, the confirmation that new faces will be available in this test is big news. Each Neighbor in Petit Planet is a character, with their own personalty and life story.

The Starsea Voyage now includes a map, too, which you can use to take you to other Islets. If you played any of the previous tests, you should already be familiar with this feature.

The only bit of bad news here is that this remains a closed beta. You’re still encouraged to sign up on the official website, but you’re not guaranteed access. HoYoverse said that only a portion of players who sign up will be invited to the upcoming beta.

Petit Planet remains without a release date. If nothing else, it’ll be interesting to see the progress the game has made since last November’s beta.

#4150. Boltgun 2 and Warhammer Survivors devs Auroch Digital say they're laying off 25% of their staff in now-deleted posts

Not long after releasing boomer shooter Warhammer 40,000: Boltgun II and right before Warhammer Survivors launches in November, developers Auroch Digital have unfortunately given a public statement confirming that roughly a quarter of its current staff will be laid off as part of a restructuring. What's strange — to the point that layoffs are, unfortunately, expected — is that the initial social media posts, on both LinkedIn and Twitter, have now been deleted.

In the studio's statement, posted yesterday, Auroch notes their pride in Boltgun II and Starship Troopers: Ultimate Bug War, both released this year, but "despite that creative success, the same market conditions that have challenged so many of our fellow developers have now also affected us." Apologies to the staff affected follow, with a plea "to partners and friends in the industry: if you are hiring, please consider finding a place for our staff in your studio. They have worked on everything from indie shooters to AAA [co-development], and their talent and breadth is second-to-none." The studio also confirms that post-launch development on both Boltgun II and Warhammer Survivors will continue despite the loss of staff.

This is, sadly, not an uncommon thing to report on by any means. There are layoffs every goddamn week, if not several. This is unique, though, in that in the time between the post going up yesterday and my writing of this piece, the public statements have been deleted. There's an archive of the original image posted here, as you won't find it on Auroch's Twitter or LinkedIn anymore. Even with the barrage of layoff news, I can't think of another time that a statement has been outright retracted within a day. Whether this was posted in error, too early, or some other reason I can't know of, hopefully there'll be some clarity soon and, more importantly, opportunities available for the staff affected.

RPS have reached out to Auroch Digital for comment and clarification.

If you like what you play, then your progress will carry over into a full PS5 game purchase. From tomorrow, the Deluxe Edition of 007 First Light will go on sale in the PS Store Black Friday promotion, so you'll be able to pick it up cheaper than full price.

The social media post confirming the Game Trial states it's open to "all PlayStation Plus members", but this isn't actually true. Game Trials are only found on the PS Plus Premium tier.

007 First Light is one of our favourites from 2026, with our PS5 review concluding: "The characterisation of this young Bond and his associates is really strong, and the globetrotting story lets you explore some great locations. #4148. Heartopia celebrates 30 million downloads with new outfits, permanent price cuts

Heartopia's rise has continued since its launch earlier this year, and the game's developer isn't slowing down with updates.

Heartopia has kicked off a new event to celebrate passing 30 million downloads. Just a couple of weeks after delivering the vintage Hollywood-themed Dreamlight Cinematics event, developer XD Games has revealed The Whimsical Tea Party, a limited-time Gilded Acorn Exhibition.

The event kicked off on Saturday, bringing some new themed content to the game.

Whimsical Tea Party’s biggest addition are the new outfits, including the Wandering Traveler, and the Duke Bunny outfits. Each outfit is available in three different colours. Another thing Heartopia events bring are building materials sets.

This one adds the Labyrinth furniture building materials set, the Hedgehog & Flamingo mallet, and the Cheshire Cat pet costume. Speaking of outfits, XD Games is dropping the in-game prices for a number of items permanently.

All original pet outfits now cost 66.7% less. Those of the Common variety will now cost 10 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, instead of the previous 30. Rare pet outfits will cost 5 Souvenir Ticket Stubs, down from 15.

If you happened to buy Common or Rare original pet outfits between July 17, 2024 and March 22, 2026, you’ll be refunded the difference. This will automatically show up in-game the next time you log in. If you instead purchased those pet outfits between March 23 and April 4, you should look forward to your refund before April 10.

Keeping with the theme of freebies, Heartopia is also celebrating surpassing 30 million downloads worldwide by giving all players a small gift package in-game. This freebie is available until May 29, so you should have enough time to claim it.

For comprehensive guidance on where to find birds, bugs, and fish, check out our Heartopia bird locations, Heartopia bug locations, and Heartopia fish locations guides. If you’re instead looking to find some wild vegetables for those cooking recipes, hit those links. And, as ever, it doesn’t hurt to see if you missed out on any Heartopia codes.

#4147. Gallery: I Spent £40 On Japanese Chocolate And All I Got Was This Zelda Merch

Japan is living in the future - quite literally.

As I wander the neon-soaked streets of Akihabara this evening, it strikes me that I'm nine hours closer to The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time's release than any of you poor sods back in Blighty. In fact, by the time you read this, I'll probably already be playing Link's latest. Sorry not sorry.

I honestly hadn't planned to be in Japan for the Ocarina launch - it sort of just happened that way. I'm glad, though; I've always dreamed of being in Tokyo's Electric Town for a moment like this.

Like, imagine being here when the clock struck midnight for the PS2's launch? I would have been sooooo happy!!! OR I would have failed to appreciate the present moment for what it was and only realised how special it was years later through a lens of nostalgia and with a tinge of sadness, while hopelessly fantasising about another time and/or a different life? Anyone else??? No, okay, sweet.

ANYWAY, while the advent of internet shopping seems to have robbed us of the very concept of the midnight launch (I can't find one for Ocarina anywhere in Tokyo), there's still an excitement in the air befitting a release of this magnitude.

Zelda is everywhere. From neighbourhood game stores to subway screens and bus stops, it's genuinely hard to miss.

Like when the trailer plays out to a captive audience on the heaving Yamanote Line. Or when audio from the Zelda Direct gets pumped into the streets outside electrical giant EDION. Or when I stumble across the biggest gaming section I've ever seen in my life (in a place called Yodobashi Akiba) and Ocarina has about five sections dedicated to it.

It's wild stuff. And it's not just the enthusiast stores getting involved, either; there's Zelda stuff in every Lawson I enter.

For the uninitiated, Lawson is a konbini (convenience store) that sells the best egg sandwich you'll ever have in your life. And some other things, I'm told. But mainly the egg sandwich.

With over 1,600 stores in Tokyo alone, it’s part of everyday life for pretty much every single city-dwelling Japanese person. So when Nintendo suggested taking over one of Lawson's Akihabara stores and plastering it with Ocarina of Time art and 40th Anniversary merch, a money expert man probably said, “Yes, that is a very good idea for making lots of money.”

Just like it was a good idea for Japanese chocolatier Lotte to partner up with Ninty on a promo campaign that's made this writer's wallet £40 lighter and waistline two inches thicker overnight.

It goes thusly: for a limited time, anyone who buys three eligible Lotte products can receive one of eight clear sleeves featuring artwork from the series’ most beloved entries.

Now, with there being eight different designs, that would mean purchasing 24 boxes of chocolate, which only a complete idiot would do hi-I'm-Rory-nice-to-meet-ya.

Honestly though, these slender sleeves prove the perfect souvenir; my bag is already bursting with merch from Nintendo Kyoto, plushes from three different Pokémon Centres, and a mint-condition Lime Green DSi I picked up for £38. God bless the struggling yen.

But as I head to Narita Airport (I leave tomorrow and I don't want to talk about it) and see the reviews come rolling in, I can't help but feel Nintendo has another mega hit on their hands with this game.

#4146. "Mass Effect was my ultimate white whale": Journey composer shares 20 minutes of music created during talks to work on BioWare's recently cancelled RPG

"It's been hard to see dear friends lose their jobs, and this beloved franchise seemingly vanish forever"

The gradual drip of details about and glimpses at what BioWare were looking to cook up with the cancelled Mass Effect 5 continues, this time thanks to a composer who was in talks to come aboard to put together the RPG's soundtrack. Said songsmith, Austin Wintory, has opted to share around 20 minutes of tunes he put together just as an attempt to explore where he might take things if he did end up being hired to score Commander Shepard's next adventure. Naturally, with BioWare's closure, that hasn't come to pass.

The eight tracks in the YouTube video Wintory, whose compositions have graced the likes of Journey and Assassin's Creed Syndicate, has put together range from a main theme, to intense battle tunes, and the sorts of 'ooh, there's something happening' songs that usually accompany key story moments. The opener, dubbed The Legacy of Shepard, blends pensive piano tinkling with bombastic sci-fi swells. The final track's a funkier remixed version of it. I think my favorite might be track seven, Forever Calibrating, just because it's the sort of relaxed and atmospheric backing tune I tend to put on for ambience while working.

"Working on Mass Effect 5 was my career's biggest dream project, my white whale," Wintory wrote in the video's description. "It is my favorite franchise of all time, and for the last couple years I'd been in serious conversations with BioWare and EA to jump in. My suggestion was to treat the original game's masterful Jack Wall/Sam Hulick score as a starting point, and to build on it from there with deeper use of physical, analog synths and a more tightly interwoven use of the orchestra. But a love letter first and foremost (not unlike my approach to the Aliens franchise with Fireteam Elite).

"As part of the ongoing dialogue, I decided last year (2025) to surprise the folks with an elaborate production: nearly 20 minutes of music, fully recorded and produced with synths, vocals and a large orchestra here in LA. I'd not yet learned any narrative details of what they were planning so this was just pure musical exploration. Receiving the news alongside everyone else that EA had decided to not only cancel the project but shutdown BioWare entirely was a deeply felt loss. It's been hard to see dear friends lose their jobs, and this beloved franchise seemingly vanish forever."

The composer closed by thanking BioWare and EA's music department for giving him the chance to put together these experimental Mass Effect tracks.

While this outpouring of info about what BioWare were up to with Mass Effect 5 is likely all we'll ever get of it, given the folks who were working on it have been scattered to the winds, some fans of the series have begun petitioning for Shep's space adventures not to end up rotting in EA's big shed of disused game IP. Though, surprisingly, they appear not to be teaming that call with the assertion that it should ideally be the same devs who were working on the series prior to BioWare's closure that get first dibs on any opportunity to carry on making Mass Effects.

#4145. Xbox Set A New Record For Game Releases In October, With Extremely Impressive Support For Play Anywhere

It's no secret that a whole bunch of new releases have been moving their release dates from November back to September and October in recent months, and it's actually resulted in a new record being set for Series X and S in 2026.

As shared by the folks behind the Xbox news for Koreans account on social media, there were 208 games released across Xbox Series X and S (and Xbox One in some cases) in October 2026, which represents the "peak month" for this year. September is second with 187 releases, and April is third with 169 releases.

Of those 208 games last month, 45% were Xbox Play Anywhere enabled, which is a pretty incredible percentage!

As you can see, the Play Anywhere percentage has been as high as 50% in 2026, and it's raised quite considerably compared to the figures we were seeing in the first few months of the year.

This clearly indicates that Xbox is ramping up the push to get as many games as possible integrated into the programme, and we're here for it - it's always incredible to get a free PC copy on top of your Series X and S purchase!

November will be much quieter for new releases with GTA 6 hogging the spotlight of course, and December should see things slow down considerably as well. As we approach the new year though, it looks like we can expect well over 1,000 new releases on Xbox Series X|S in 2027 once again, with maybe around half of them getting Xbox Play Anywhere support along the way. Bring it on!

#4144. Ubisoft One of Multiple Companies to Bid for Dishonored Dev Arkane

Ubisoft is one of multiple companies to submit a bid for Dishonored team Arkane Studios, as Microsoft looks to offload the developer in the coming weeks.

That's according to Bloomberg journalist Jason Schreier, who claims that at least two other gaming firms have tried to acquire the developer. No deal has been agreed with Microsoft yet, and Xbox has also weighed up "selling the studio to its management".

Any potential deal is likely to include Arkane being allowed to finish its development of Marvel's Blade, according to the Bloomberg piece, which is set for release in the next year or two. A PS5 version of the game has never been confirmed.

Previously, a cut-off point regarding any potential deal involving Arkane Studios was set for 13th November 2026. That has now been extended by a month, however, to 13th December. Schreier has previously stated he is confident a deal will be struck for Arkane to continue existing under a different owner.

News Microsoft Gives Dishonored Dev More Time to Find a Buyer, Needs a Partner to Finish Blade

#4143. Honkai: Star Rail players are eating good, with Version 4.2 and third anniversary celebrations kicking off later this month

Honkai: Star Rail will be celebrating its third anniversary just days after it delivers a major update, and there's quite a bit to chew on in this one.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a stacked Honkai: Star Rail Special Program, delivering the one-two punch of revealing the game’s next major update, and detailing what you can expect from its third anniversary celebrations.

First off, Version 4.2, dubbed So Laughed the Masses, arrives April 22, making two characters playable, and bringing back a host of beloved characters for re-runs. The new update continues the Phantasmoon Games arc, as the story takes an especially suspect new development.

The big inciting incident of this new chapter is the reveal that whoever wins the Phantasmoon Games will also become the permanent Aeon of Elation. Meanwhile, Fulwish has invited all Supplicants to the Fulwish TV HQ to announce their intention to host a TV debate about the ultimate goal of the Phantasmoon Games.

Naturally, you’re invited, and you’ll have to overcome the challenges that await to gather more Wishpower.

Our first new arrival is Silver Wolf LV.999, with whom you should already be familiar from her Version 1 form. The difference now, of course, is that she’s getting a brand-new alternate kit, since — true to her new name — she's evolved into a Godmode Player upon reaching Level 999. Silver Wolf LV.999 is a 5-Star Imaginary character on the Path of Elation.

Her main combat trick is the ability to rack up Hidden MMR, which is what allows her to eventually activate her Cartridge and settle into the aforementioned Godmode state. While in that form, she shifts the entire battle into the virtual world, pulling in both teams into her gaming domain.

This is essentially a world under her control, which is why she can unlock a Reward Stage at the start of her turn, which lets her spawn in-game items. When picked up, these items can turn the tide of battle.

Keeping up with the ultra-gamer persona, Silver Wolf's Aha Instant strike blasts all enemies with a laser cannon, dealing massive damage. Perhaps her most interesting ability is being able to hack into the battlefield when she’s not actively on the team, something she can do when a teammate falls under enemy control.

Evanescia is the other newly-playable character, who has thus far only been an observer of the Phantasmoon Games, as well as one of the most prominent new characters we've met so far on Planarcadia. V4.2 sees the girl join the roster as a 5-Star Physical character who’s likewise on the Path of Elation. As she fights, she always accumulates Certified Banger, when she earns the title she’s able to simultaneously regenerate Energy and maintain her damage.

Evanescia’s damage continues to increase the more Certified Banger she accumulates, triggering an attack from Master Fox upon reaching a certain threshold, which deals damage to all enemies and regenerates Energy for herself. Her Elation Skill adds a bit of a performance to her kit, and is capable of hitting all enemies.

You may have noticed the Path of Elation theme in this one, so you won’t be surprised to learn that the Elation Trailblazer variant on the main playable character is also joining the team in 4.2. There’s a new weapon that starts off as a glow stick but can transform into a lightblade as you deal damage, and, yes, gain Certified Banger.

It can also turn into nunchucks, which delivers a unique flurry of attacks on all enemies surrounding the character, dealing multiple instances of damage. You can also use it to cheer for a teammate, hyping them up.

Version 4.2 Warp Events will bring back six characters. The first half will see reruns of The Dahlia, Castorice, and Firefly. The second half will give you another shot at unlocking Tribbie, Sunday, and Feixiao. What’s more, four of the game’s characters will be buffed in this update, so you may want to reconsider putting them them back on your team. They are Firefly, Huohuo, Seele, and Welt.

As part of the same update, you can expect the debut of the Cosmic Data Roaming event, which goes live alongside the anniversary celebrations. The event lets you live the life of a streamer.

Currency Wars is getting a big expansion, too. Likewise, the Cosmicon Collective is getting its version 2.0 update, adding new decks, dice as well as a new team challenge game mode.

As for the big third anniversary celebration, it will kick off in-game on April 26, bringing back Festive Gifts. The event will only be available during these celebrations, and it will once again be gifting players who log in regularly a total of 20 pulls.

You’ll also be able to a select a blessing card from a companion of your choice to receive a special gift of 1,600 Stellar Jades. The same celebrations will also seeHuohuo and Robin permanently added to the Stellar Convergence store. You’ll have another chance to exchange a Golden Companion Spirit for any companion you like in that store, too — and all you need to do is log in anytime between Versions 4.2 and 4.4. This being a new year for Honkai: Star Rail, the top-up double bonus is resetting, meaning anyone who tops up their wallet will get a hefty bonus.

Elsewhere, you’ll find new items in the Gift of Stardust Store, including a new outfit for Castorice. Between the time 4.2 launches and when the celebrations begin, you’ll be able to try your luck in Aha's Chosen: Spreading Elation Everywhere, an online event where you can leave a message for a chance to win various prizes.

#4142. Animal Crossing: New Horizons gets a new item to celebrate 25 years of the series

The allegedly finished game might finally, truly be feature complete with the addition of an anniversary item.

Animal Crossing: New Horizons has received a surprise patch today to celebrate the 25th anniversary of the life sim series. The update, version 3.0.2, is available across the Switch and Switch 2 versions of the game.

The patch brings a single new addition to New Horizons - a leaf item. Everyone gets it, too, so you don’t have to do anything special to acquire it.

After installing the patch, simply head to your in-house mailbox to claim it. The mail includes a hearty message to fans who supported the series for years, featuring an appropriate Nintendo N64 stamp.

The Leaf Statue, as it’s referred to in-game, lights up when placed.

April 14, 2011 marks the release of the original, lesser-known version of Animal Crossing in Japan. The game was initially released as Animal Forest (Dobutsu no Mori) on the Nintendo N64, before later making its way to the Nintendo GameCube in December of the same year as Dobutsu no Mori+ with some extra features.

That same, original design of the package is also available for display in your game. The rest of the patch notes are entirely about various bug fixes, so not much more there. You can see the full change log on Nintendo’s support website.

#4141. Countdown: Zelda: Ocarina Of Time Dungeon Crawl #9 - The Grand Finale

Now yes, I know I said this series was going to work on a weekly basis, but as we hit launch week, I suddenly realised that this wouldn't give me time to touch on the big finale. And that wouldn't do! I've recapped everything from the Great Deku Tree to the Spirit Temple - did you really think I'd be able to stop without a nod to the last challenge of them all?

And so, welcome to the final edition of my Ocarina of Time Dungeon Crawl. I've awakened all the Sages, finished all the dungeons and now it's finally time to put the big bad to bed. Just in time to do it all again.

Review The Legend Of Zelda: Ocarina Of Time (Switch 2) - A Stunning Remake, But Not Quite Definitive

As with every other entry in my replay series, I'm going into endgame spoilers here, so turn back now if you've been saving yourself for the remake!

I didn't think of Ganondorf's Castle as a 'proper' Ocarina of Time dungeon because of its size, but returning to it on this playthrough may have changed my mind. Sure, it's on the shorter side, but it has a boss key, unique puzzle rooms, a big fight at the end, and even a unique item found within. This is definitely a dungeon.

And what a great way to wrap things up. I love the unique temple rooms, each based on mechanics that you have learnt from the game up to this point. Each one feels like a fitting send-off to the dungeons that inspired them without retracing steps that we've taken before. Even though I did the Spirit Temple last, its respective room in the Castle always makes me smile with its Bombchu-shaped hole in the top of the cage.

None of the rooms outstay their welcome, either. They serve as a nice little reminder of how far you have come and then get out of there before things start feeling repetitive. Finishing the 'Light' room only to find the final orb not where you expect it to be and a liminal extra tunnel in its place (only seen with the Lens of Truth) freaked me out back in the day, so that was a nice bit of resurfaced trauma for me when I came to it this time.

Powering down the beams is an easy enough process, and it's only amped up on the ensuing staircase ascent. Splitting the grand finale into puzzle and combat gauntlets is a really great idea, and it works wonders here. I don't like facing off against two sword-wielding enemies simultaneously any more than the next man, but it suitably ramps up the stakes as I get ever closer to the top floor and the ominous piano music.

And what a treat it is when you finally get to the top. This is high camp. You can't tell me that Ganondorf perfectly whacking out an overture on the keys while Princess Zelda floats over him is anything but. It's a foundational memory, and it rules.

For all of its grandeur, I still find the initial 'tennis' fight a little on the easy side (after restarting when I realised I had foolishly got greedy on the penultimate floor and needlessly gobbled up all the Green Potions, leaving me none for a mid-battle refill). It's epic, and a fitting throwback to the Phantom fight all those hours ago, but a little more attack deviation wouldn't have gone amiss.

With Link winning game-set-match, it was time for things to get cinematic. There's something about the N64 Rumble Pak going ham as the castle crumbles that never fails to tickle me. The falling effect looks naff in 2026, but I don't care. The final escape is still as tense as anything, and I always cheer when the top floor finally hits the ground.

But, of course, I wasn't done. All of my issues with the simplicity of the Ganondorf fight go out the window in the final 'Boar' battle.

On paper, it's just as straightforward as the previous phase — roll between the legs, hit the tail, repeat — but it just feels so damn cool doing it! I didn't have time for side quests in this playthrough, so I polished off the majority of the fight with the Megaton Hammer instead (the first time I've ever done so, I think). So yes, running over to re-collect the Master Sword and deliver the final blow at the end felt all the better for it.

And just like that, the game was complete. I lose track of how many times I have watched the finale by this point. It always makes me weep.

When I first played, I was rooting for Link to go back to his old time and catch up on the childhood that he'd missed. Now that I'm older (much older than 'Adult' Link is supposed to be), there was a faint pang in my heart when I realised that he'd never see the world he'd saved or the lives he'd pushed back on track.

I had forgotten how quickly things cut to the credits as Zelda plays her final lullaby, but let it be known, I was a wreck as the devs' names rolled by.

As a victory lap of everything that has come before it, Inside Ganon's Castle doesn't really put a foot wrong. It's a brief one, and the final head-to-head isn't quite as intense as I remembered it, but man, it doesn't get much more epic than this.

I can't wait to cry my eyes out all over again in the coming days weeks on Switch 2.

That's yer lot! To those who have followed this Dungeon Crawl series from the beginning, thank you for joining me on this replay. To those who only just dropped in for the finale, there's eight weeks' worth of catching up to do!

#4140. Steam Frame kernel updated with external CD-ROM drive compatibility just one day after a user asked Valve for it

Even with the importance of physical media ownership in the current era of digital product ephemera, it's often unlikely your PC will actually be able to play the CDs, DVDs or Blu-Rays you have around the house. Internal disc drives aren't common amongst desktops or even laptops anymore, so your only recourse is often an external drive.

One Steam Frame user was hoping to connect his own detachable disc drive to watch movies and play Need For Speed Carbon (valid!) using the headset, which can run both VR and 'flat' games without a separate PC, but found that the Frame lacked the drivers to read a disc. In a very earnest community post, user Aiodensghost lamented that this fact "KILLED MY ABILITY TO INSTALL MY ABANDONWARE FROM 2006. You don't sell NFS Carbon anymore (fuck you very much EA) [...] May I PLEASE have the ability to use an optical drive?" So polite!

A Valve employee by the username gaberowe would respond a day later, simply saying "we will look into this thanks for alerting us". Around ten minutes pass, and the 'deckard-linux-no-oopsies' GitHub repository (yes, it's really called that), which is the Linux kernel sources used in SteamOS for the Steam Frame, sees a commit from Rowe that effectively turns on CD-ROM support. More savvy Steam Frame users can hypothetically install the updated kernel themselves, as this commit enabled an existing Linux kernel feature, but it's likely that this support will simply be added in an upcoming software update.

In a news role where I am continually reporting on generative AI and layoffs, it's nice to report on something that boils down to 'software developer does something cool, quickly.' And, hey, Aiodensghost can play Need For Speed Carbon despite EA, which is always a gift.

#4139. Metro 2039 goes back to its Metro underground roots, with a story shaped by the war in Ukraine and the people who suffer it

Metro 2039 takes us back to the tunnels of the Moscow Metro where, fittingly, Nazi ideology never died.

The Metro series is finally, officially back with a new installment. 4A Games has just unveiled Metro 2039 to the world, the follow-up to the outstanding Metro Exodus, released all the way back in 2019.

2039 takes an unusual route with its scope, however. Rather than build on the semi-open-world structure of Exodus, the upcoming sequel instead brings the focus back to where it all began: the Metro.

What won’t be changing is the kind of game that it is. Metro 2039 remains, like its predecessors, a story-driven, single-player game. Returning to the confined spaces of the Moscow Metro brings the focus back to the claustrophobic, uneasy atmosphere of the original games.

The game’s protagonist is, for the first time, going to be voiced throughout. From what we’ve been able to see, the psychological horror in this installment will be driven more by the very real effects the apocalypse has had, and continues to have, on denizens of the Metro.

2039 has been in development for years, but 4A Games has been rocked by two considerable events: the 2020 Covid pandemic, and Russia’s 2022 invasion of Ukraine, where the developer is based. The game’s darker story has changed in response to that.

The team’s Ukrainian perspective is molded into the narrative, and more prominently represents the toll the events of the last several years has taken on members of the team, their families and communities.

According to the developer, you can expect a bigger emphasis on choice and consequence, with Russian author Dmitry Glukhovsky returning to co-write a narrative that explores the compromised morality of a post-war society.

The new protagonist’s return to the Metro comes with the reveal that the different underground factions are now united under one banner, the not-so-subtly named Novoreich. Lead by a former Spartan, the Novoreich is an authoritarian regime which offers what it believes to be the only path to salvation.

4A Games remains majority Ukrainian, with teams based in Kyiv, and Malta. Unlike most AAA projects today, the studio continues to rely on its own engine tech. The 4A Engine is given a major upgrade for 2039: ray tracing is now a core component of the rendering pipeline, but the tech has been rebuilt to run better on modern hardware.

Today’s reveal sadly didn’t feature much gameplay - only a brief first-look with a mix of gameplay and cinematics. The developer, however, emphasised that creating cluttered, believable and lived-in environments remains a key focus.

Metro 2039 is set for release sometime this winter on PC, Xbox Series X/S, and PS5.

#4138. PS Store Black Friday Sale Live Now with 2,200+ PS5 Discounts

PS5 and PS4 games going cheap we recommend

It's time for the Black Friday sale on PS Store, running from now through to 30th November, 2026.

As with nearly every offer in Sony's digital store, there are literally thousands of PS5 and PS4 games going cheap. Obviously, nobody has the time to scroll through all those deals, which is where this guide (hopefully) comes in handy.

We've put together a list of some of the games we'd highly recommend while they're on offer.

Everything listed here comes with at least a 7/10 score from Push Square, and every game is at its lowest price point, with some setting new lows in this sale.

Discounted prices are shown in bold, and games at a new lowest-ever price are bold and underlined.

If you need to top up your PSN wallet, we've got you covered:

Please note that some external links on this page are affiliate links, which means if you click them and make a purchase we may receive a small percentage of the sale. Please read our FTC Disclosure for more information.

Buy Sony PlayStation Network Wallet Top-Up

Let's have a look at some of the best games in the Planet of the Deals sale.

1000xRESIST is all in on story, and this laser focus allows it to tell one of the most captivating and intriguing experiences you can have in video games. This sci-fi adventure sees an alien disease almost wipe out humanity, but one person is immune, and they rebuild society underground by cloning her. Combining visual novel elements with exploration, it's not the most challenging game to play, but its narrative more than makes it worthwhile.

If you're looking for a chilled out puzzle game to wind down with, A Monster's Expedition comes highly recommended. It's one of those puzzlers with a seemingly straightforward set of mechanics, but it uses them in increasingly smart ways to really test your brainpower. Set across hundreds of tiny islands you need to navigate by pushing logs into the water, its forgiving nature and gentle presentation make it a lovely game to get lost in.

A whimsical, miniature open world awaits in A Short Hike. From a top-down perspective, you explore an island with lots of interesting places to visit and adorable characters, each of whom has a task for you. This laid back experience is a true joy as you gain new abilities, collect things, and discover new areas.

Absolum is both a brilliantly crafted beat-'em-up and a devilishly addictive roguelike. Although the overall experience does feel slightly short-lived, you'll seriously struggle to tear yourself away from the game's striking fantasy world — especially when all of its systems start to click.

Arranger: A Role-Puzzling Adventure is a delightfully inventive puzzle game that weaves in a neat narrative to pull you through. Playing as a character that literally moves the world around her as she goes, this is effectively a series of slide puzzles set within a fleshed out world full of whimsical character. Always building on its core idea in imaginative ways, this is brilliant fun from start to finish.

Building upon the great foundations laid in Astro's Playroom, Astro Bot is the full-blown 3D platformer the little robot deserves. It's an explosion of creativity and fun; there is something new to discover in practically every level, and all of it is purpose built to put a smile on your face. Not only is it bursting with imagination, it's also executed brilliantly. The controls are spot on, every new mechanic and power-up is fun to use, and it's all presented with incredibly sharp visuals and flawless performance. The icing on the cake is its celebration of PlayStation's past 30 years, with delightful nods to hundreds of classics. We can't recommend this highly enough.

While many of the included games may border on unplayable from a modern perspective, the painstaking attention to detail in Atari 50: The Anniversary Celebration is extremely easy to appreciate. The museum-like carousel of content, from interviews through to original artwork, is presented so handsomely that you can’t not get swept up in Atari’s dramatic story. And the fact that there over 100 of the company’s most famous titles, emulated excellently with their original instruction manuals available to pore over, adds playable context to a lot of the content. This is just an impressive overall experience that will appeal to those who lived through the rise (and fall) of Atari, as well as younger players eager to learn a little more about one of the industry’s true pioneers.

Ball X Pit is a dangerously addictive roguelite that combines the speedy runs and rapid leveling up of Vampire Survivors with the ball-bouncing action of Breakout. It's one of those concepts that'll make you question why a game like it hasn't been done before, because it works brilliantly. Every element of the game feeds into something else, and the result is this incredibly compelling game that has a surprising amount to see and do.

Battle Chef Brigade Deluxe is the definitive version of this unusual but great culinary adventure. Set in a world where chefs go head-to-head in a prestigious cooking tournament, the game is half action title and half cooking minigames. You'll go out slaying monsters and harvesting ingredients, then brew them up to create delicious dishes to satisfy the judges. It's an odd recipe, but results in a surprisingly tasty dish.

A true cult classic, Beyond Good & Evil: 20th Anniversary Edition is a lovely remaster of a PS2 favourite. Playing as freedom fighter Jade, this unique sci-fi adventure has you exploring a weird and wonderful world through the lens of her camera. The remaster brings the visuals up to date and throws in some quality-of-life improvements, but the main reason to play this is for the great story and characters, which remain fresh and charming to this day.

Broken Sword: Shadow of the Templars is a sacred text in the history of point-and-click adventure games, and new remaster Reforged is the best version of the game that's ever been released. Quality-of-life improvements mean players who just want to enjoy the story without too much lateral thinking can do so, while veterans of the genre or returning fans can play the game in its original form, goats and all. Paris in the fall has never been more beautiful.

There have been climbing games before, but Cairn is a really unique example. To scale the huge Mount Kami, you need to control Aava's limbs individually, looking out for the best holds as you inch upward. On top of the challenging, physics-based mountaineering, you also need to keep on top of her health and hunger, but these survival aspects never feel too overbearing. It's a nicely balanced game with climbing that feels tangible and realistically tough.

Half interactive story, half cube-based puzzler, Catherine: Full Body is the expanded remaster of Atlus' brilliantly weird take on love. You play as Vincent, a 32-year-old bachelor who can't quite decide if he wants to commit to his long-term girlfriend. His potential infidelity gives way to suspiciously vivid nightmares where he's forced to scramble up towers made of blocks, lest he wake up dead. It's as mental as it sounds, but the tactile puzzles are addictive, and the storytelling is gripping at its best.

Stephen has been part of the Push Square team for over six years, bringing boundless enthusiasm and a deep knowledge of video games to his role as Assistant Editor. Having grown up playing every PlayStation console to date, he's developed an eclectic taste, with particular passion for indie games, arcade racers, and puzzlers. He's also our go-to guy for Sonic-related matters, much to his delight/chagrin.

#4137. Life is Strange makers Don't Nod face layoffs and possible insolvency, French workers union STJV state

Le Syndicat des Travailleureuses du Jeu Vidéo, a French game workers union, have released a statement detailing the current status of Don't Nod, the studio behind Life is Strange and Lost Records: Bloom and Rage. The studio's fate has been precarious for some time, but STJV now say that the studio has announced ("to financial press before the employees, as has been its MO") that it is under a "safeguard procedure" to avoid complete insolvency due to an inability to pay off its debts.

The studio's CEO, Oskar Guilbert, told employees that "a safeguarding process is an act of anticipation", in reference to the fact that last year, the CSE (employee representatives) were presented with two outcomes: either future games would find funding and staff would still be laid off, or no funding would be acquired, and the company would be liquidated. It seems the latter is now likely to come to pass, as STJV state that the company does not even have the funds to complete its pre-existing redundancies plan for laid-off employees. The union also note that "the CEO finished his address with empty remarks on how much attention was paid to employees, which everyone knows was bullshit and probably written by ChatGPT."

The statement goes on to clarify that the company will be unable to complete the last remaining project that was in development, referred to as P14. This is due to a huge incoming swathe of layoffs, which include "nearly all of the non-managerial jobs":

"6/6 animators, 3/3 character artists, 3/3 concept artists, 8/10 environmental artists, 2/3 sound designers, 4/8 game designers, 3/5 level designers, 6/6 associate producers, 18/22 programmers, 3/5 QA testers, 2/3 devops, 3/4 HR…

"Management is extremely clearly going for heavily individualized targeting and hasn’t been shy about their intent to keep selected people in rather than jobs, which is illegal."

In an apparent attempt to keep the studio running despite obliterating its staff, "management is betting its all on outsourcing", expecting managers to be able to keep things moving as normal despite the alleged shift to outsourcing and contractors taking on the existing work of fired staff. STJV put it better than I could: "Anyone with a little experience with video games production and sanity understands how out-of-touch such a plan is. The costs of outsourcing a project that was mostly internal up until now and the loss of the experience gained all throughout production seem to have been ignored in favour of short-term penny-pinching with unclear upsides."

The article closes by claiming that the CSE's negotiations with Don't Nod were essentially a farce, as the company had no intent of negotiating in the first place; "Management declares that it cannot offer anything: it’ll be the strict legal minimum and you’ll be glad for it." Concerns regarding the future of the studio have seemingly been made clear by the CSE for years, reportedly living with a sword of Damocles over their heads due to repeated mismanagement, miscommunication and gaslighting, but the future looks bleak. "They ignored the CSE, middle managers, the STJV, financial auditors, all because they believed unyieldingly that a miracle would come and they’d find funds for a game that was too big, too ambitious and ultimately too expensive."

The CSE consultation will reach its end on November 3rd, following which "the regional agency for employment and industry will have 21 days to decide on the plan, and if it is accepted, people could get their firing letters on November 25th." Though, if it is rejected, management would have to figure out a way forward other than insolvency, "because, as you might have gathered, planning for contingencies isn’t their forte."

#4136. Blizzard will talk about Diablo 4: Lord of Hatred one last time before the expansion's launch next week

We're well under two weeks from the launch of Diablo 4's next expansion, Lord of Hatred, but there's more yet to be said.

Diablo 4 is mere days away from the launch of its biggest expansion yet, and Blizzard wants to make sure it got one last chance to tell you about it. Lord of Hatred is the follow-up to 2024’s Vessel of Hatred, and it’s set to arrive on April 28.

Next week, however, we’re getting an updated look at the new content as part of a livestream. This is the Developer Update kind; the meaty, information-dense show anyone who follows Diablo’s livestreams should be familiar with.

The next Developer Update is set for Thursday, April 23. It’ll kick off at 11am PT, 2pm ET, 6pm GMT. The show will, naturally, focus on Lord of Hatred. In particular, we’re getting another look at the expansion content that hasn’t been given the same level of coverage as the bigger features.

Everyone knows about the new Skovos region, the Warlock class (and the Paladin before that), but we haven’t seen much from the other gameplay-altering features that affect a lot of the core flow.

In next week’s showcase, Blizzard will show off the updated and expanded skill trees - which come to all classes, the Talisman system, and the gear-altering Horadric Cube. War Plans, the new make-your-own-endgame feature will be discussed, too.

More interestingly, we’re also going to hear about the new season kicking off right alongside the launch of Lord of Hatred. A short, in-betweener season is currently live in Diablo 4, and it’s going to end right as the next one/the expansion launch.

And, of course, the show won’t end before the team takes a few questions from chat, as is tradition. If you want to catch it live, you’ll be able to do so on Diablo’s official YouTube, Twitch, Twitter, and TikTok channels.

#4135. Xbox's New 25 Years Bundle Retails For $569.99, And Here's The Full List Of Games

Update: Microsoft has removed the ability to purchase it

Update [Wed 4th Nov 2026, 2:45pm]: Microsoft has now quietly removed the ability to buy this bundle. It still exists on the store for eligible PC buyers as a freebie, but the price tag has been taken away - at least for the time being.

Original Story: Last week, you may recall that we ran a story about how Xbox was giving away 25 free games to eligible buyers of Windows 11 PCs, and that the offer was technically supposed to begin on November 2nd (but had begun slightly early).

Well, last night, the "25 Years of XBOX Bundle" suddenly appeared on the Microsoft Store with an actual price tag, meaning that even if you aren't eligible to get the games for free, you can actually buy the bundle if you really want to.

Just one problem - it's retailing for a whopping $569.99.

Its existence on the Microsoft Store also means we have the full list of included games, which is as follows:

Now, as much as there are some excellent games in the list here, it's hard to recommend paying anywhere near $569.99 for them. We reckon that's not really the point though — the bundle was created as a generous freebie for new Windows 11 PC buyers after all. It's also only available in the United States.

Should you wish to go ahead and get it anyway, you'll obviously be able to play all 25 of them on PC, while around half include the Xbox One / Series X|S versions via Play Anywhere, such as Gears of War: Reloaded and DOOM + DOOM 2.

We reckon it's only worth picking up if you fall into the "eligible" freebie bracket, which unfortunately still remains quite vague when looking at the official FAQ for the 25 years of XBOX bundle.

"Customers in the United States are eligible when they purchase and activate a qualifying new Windows PC from a participating U.S. retailer or OEM during the offer period. Eligible devices include select Windows Home PCs from participating Microsoft and OEM device lines, including qualifying handhelds. The only Windows Pro exception is a qualifying NVIDIA RTX Spark™ devices running Windows Pro. Other Windows Pro devices are not eligible. The offer is valid for qualifying purchases made between November 2, 2026, at 12:00 AM UTC and December 31, 2026, at 11:59 PM UTC, while supplies last."

We've already seen some people getting the bundle for free after buying a ROG Xbox Ally X20 in recent days, so that handheld seems to be part of the promotion, but it'd be nice if we had a proper breakdown of all the eligible devices.

Anyway, let us know what you think about this bundle in the comments down below - are you hoping to claim yours?!

#4134. The Sims 4's much maligned paid mods have made it to consoles, but Kits are coming back to PC

The Sims 4's Marketplace and user-created content have officially arrived on consoles, a little over a month after their debut on PC.

The Sims 4 players on PlayStation and Xbox have now caught up to their friends on PC, at least when it comes to the game’s Marketplace. This new feature is essentially a hub for paid mods and other user-created content.

As often happens when long-established games introduce paid mods, The Sims 4’s wasn’t especially well-received, in part because of the introduction of a new premium currency - Moola - that is the only way to purchase any of that content.

The Moola denominations and prices are similar to many other in-game currencies, and the criticism around them is the same: they obfuscate the true value of items, and because of the way those denominations are structured, you’ll never be able to buy exactly what you need.

For most games, the subject of paid mods has always been fraught, and that's certainly true for The Sims 4. In the announcement blog post, Maxis said that the launch on consoles will work similarly to what PC players have seen, in that Kits will no longer be available to buy directly with real money on the PlayStation and Microsoft Stores. While Expansion Packs, Game Packs, and Stuff Packs will remain, you’ll need to buy Moola if you want to acquire Kits going forward.

Interestingly, however, EA seems to have changed its mind somewhat on the Kits situation. A recently leaked memo (via SimsCommunity), appears to show that the publisher intends on making Kits available for purchase directly again, without the need for Moola.

Unfortunately, this only appears to affect the PC version, with the reversion reportedly forthcoming on both the EA App as well as Steam. Indeed, according to the same report, the change has already taken place on the former, with the latter following on April 20.

Considering the Marketplace only just launched on consoles, the company may wait to see if the decision to remove Kits from console platform marketplaces will be as poorly received as it has been on PC.

If you’re looking to jump back into The Sims 4 to check out all the new paid content, make sure you’re well-equipped with our list of Sims 4 cheats and debug options, or this one specifically for the Royalty & Legacy expansion cheats.

#4133. Naval warfare, an actual server browser and more on the way to Battlefield 6 this year as BF Studios reveals 2026 roadmap

2026 is looking very exciting for Battlefield 6, even if much of what's coming is based on things we already know, and some we've long been asking for.

It took Battlefield Studios over four months to tell Battlefield 6 players what they can actually expect from the game over the course of this year, in terms of content - but we’re glad to see a plan laid out nonetheless.

The developer unveiled a grand 2026 roadmap, covering three more seasons currently in the works, and a wealth of new additions across the entire game, including new maps and the introduction of a new theatre of combat.

In a wide-ranging new video dubbed The Year Ahead, members of the Battlefield 6 development team have revealed a lot of new information about the future of the multiplayer shooter, going over plenty of the features and new content coming over the course of this year.

The video confirmed that BF6 has at least three other seasons in the works. Season 3, which begins in May, will be followed by Season 4, and Season 5 later in the year. Season 5 is the most mysterious, which is understandable.

We’ve known about some of what’s coming in Season 3, such as the remake of Golmud Railway (now called Railway to Golmud), but the video also revealed that a remake of Battlefield 3’s Grand Bazaar - now Cairo Bazaar - will also arrive later in the same season. Other exciting additions, such as battle royale solos and ranked play for Redsec are also on the agenda for Season 3.

Season 4, set for July, looks to be the biggest so far, with the introduction of naval combat, which will be available across two maps. Tsuru Reef, which is said to be even larger than Golmud, the largest map in BF6. The Pacific-set map won’t be the only one, as later in the season, another remake will arrive, this time of the iconic Wake Island.

The introduction of naval combat will bring with it a new dynamic wave system, aircraft carriers with operational flight decks, and new naval vehicles. Custom lobbies and Spectator Mode are also planned for Season 4.

Season 5 will bring three maps to BF6, rather than two, but all of its content remains under wraps.

Perhaps a sour note is that almost all of the maps referenced and shown in the video are remakes of maps from other Battlefield games, or reimagined at the very least. The Battlefield series is no stranger to remaking its own maps, but Battlefield 6 appears to be leaning on it much more than past entries.

If it’s any consolation, however, the map remakes we’ve played so far in Battlefield 6 have gone through major changes that have contributed to giving them a different flow and feel from their classic versions, or even remakes in other BF games.

Over the course of 2026, you can also expect the return of persistent servers, as well as a server browser to find them all - just like the good ol’ days. This includes the ability to host your own, though it’s unclear quite how this is going to work.

Season 3 is set to revealed in the coming days, so you’ll be hearing back from BF Studios in the near future.

#4131. STALKER 2's latest update expands its A-Life NPC simulation bubble, seemingly without a scary performance tax

STALKER 2: Heart of Chornobyl has a new update out, 2.1, which builds on the excellent 2.0 patch by upgrading that most beloved and contentious of STALKER series features: the A-Life system that governs simulated NPC behavior. With the 2.1 update. It's now possible to whack up the distance at which A-Life NPCs (who, unlike scripted characters, will wander around, fight others over faction turf, and sometimes hunker down for a campfire-side guitar sesh) are visualised, while audio tweaks can make these unplanned shootouts audible from further away. The effect, in theory, is a better sense of the Zone's inhabitants going about their bang-banging business, even if Mr. Main Character here isn't close by.

Both the updated game and the accompanying blog post warn that cranking this A-Life bubble up beyond the lowest, default 'Recommended' setting may have adverse effects, ranging from lower framerates to "story quest instability" and crashes. Fearing a return to STALKER 2's bug-ridden early days, I tried out the new A-Life distance options on the RPS test rig, and found they're not actually that perilous – though they might do strange things with binoculars.

To judge the performance effect, I ran the rig's RTX 4060 at 1080p, with Quality-level DLSS and the High preset - save for having the draw distance setting on Epic, to maximise the potential visualisation. Walking through an open, A-Life-ripe patch of the Zone produced a 93fps average on Recommended, which remained unchanged on the Extended setting, before barely dropping to 91fps on the Highly Extended, Maximum and Dynamic settings. Well that's not so bad! The warnings made it sound like the bigger options would ignite the air around my graphics card and brainwarp quest NPCs into thinking they were in Barbie Horse Ride & Rescue (available now on Steam). 2fps? That's nothing. Nothing.

Granted, results may vary depending on your PC specs; the RTX 4060 isn't especially potent but it was backed up by a good CPU and a healthy 32GB of RAM, which likely helped handle the extra computations required for a wider sprawl of distant gunfights. To get a fuller picture, I did try a different approach, leaving ground level to claim a lofty concrete vantage point and- god dammit, recently added fog effects.

Still, the Zone's unknowable RNG calculations were not kind, and after several minutes of fruitless waiting I returned to run more tests on terra firma.

I ultimately didn't find anything else that would suggest an unacceptable risk of performance loss or instability, though I did discover one quirk of the new system: in addition to render distance, your choice of A-Life setting also appears to influence the range at which faction markers show up on binoculars.

More strangely, selecting Maximum A-Life also seems to… increase the zoom of binoculars? As you can see in those two shots, which were snapped from the same position. I guess it's a bug but hey, if GSC are telling me I can get better NPC simulation and a magnification upgrade for the low, low price of two frames per second, I'll take that deal.

STALKER 2 2.1 is out now for everyone. Besides the A-Life distance gubbins, it also adds the ability to tag along with roaming fellow stalkers, turning them into mobile fast travel stations - though, in keeping with the notion that NPCs don't actually give a toss about you, they'll only warp you to places that their specific patrol route was passing anyway.

#4130. Diablo 4's next season won't have any new mechanics or a new theme because all the focus is on Lord of Hatred

If you don't intend to buy the Lord of Hatred expansion, the next season in Diablo 4 won't be as exciting as you'd expect.

Diablo 4 is gearing up for its biggest post-launch event yet: the upcoming release of the Lord of Hatred expansion. As was the case with Vessel of Hatred before it, expansion releases alter the seasonal flow in a few ways, and Blizzard has now explained how.

The game’s next season - its 13th - has been officially revealed as Season of Reckoning. The new season will kick off alongside the expansion’s release next week, and will be available to all players, just like all previous seasons.

Although Season of Reckoning will roll out as normal, the season itself won’t be as meaty, at least when it comes to the sort of gameplay mechanics and themes players have come to expect from each new season.

You’ll still find the normal Season Rank chase, Smoldering Ashes, and various rewards at each chapter. Season Blessings will also return, but that’s about it for progression outside of the game itself. If it’s any consolation, there are more goals and objectives to tackle this season.

The even better news is that, according to Blizzard, future seasons will follow the classic format, which makes sense. The new season will come with a battle pass, of course, featuring four Reliquaries, as usual. The first Reliquary is free, while the others are paid.

Blizzard has also confirmed the the pre-load for Lord of Hatred is available now on all platforms. Even if you’re not getting the expansion, patch 3.0.0's pre-load includes all expansion content regardless, so you may as well pre-download it to be ready for April 27/28. On launch day, you’ll also need to download a smaller patch, version 3.0.1.

In case you missed it, we published our Lord of Hatred review earlier in the week. Give it a read if you’re curious about the expansion’s impact on the narrative, and how it changes core Diablo 4 gameplay.

#4129. Zenless Zone Zero Version 2.8 is refreshing your team comps with a new mechanic, and the game is coming to Steam

Zenless Zone Zero will soon become the first HoYoverse game to make its way to Steam, though we wish we had more details.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a pretty exciting Zenless Zone Zero Special Program that not only delivered all the details on the next big update, it also came with the unexpected announcement that the action RPG is on its way to Steam.

Previously, all HoYoverse games with PC versions have always been directly available from the developer’s website, or through the Epic Games Store. In other words, Zenless Zone Zero will soon mark the massive company’s debut on Valve’s platform.

The main focus of the livestream, of course, has been Version 2.8, otherwise known as New Eridan Sunset. This upcoming release is scheduled for May 6, though the Steam version does not yet have a date.The new release sees the release of two new Agents, as well as the brand-new Wind attribute enemy.

The release also acts as the last chapter of Season 2, and it sees Ramiel becoming the main target of different factions in the Outer Ring. The two new arrivals, together with Proxies and Cissia will embark on a quest to learn the new identity of Ramiel.

The first new Agent is Promeia, the executioner of Krampus. She’s an S-Rank Ice Anomaly Agent who can consume Trial by Cold to trigger Abloom on enemies. This is done by converting Corrosive Chill.

By using her EX Special Attack, she can enter the Bound Absolution state, which allows her to automatically Perfect Dodge any attack that targets her. If you have another Anomaly or Support Agent on the team, Promeia can further boost the entire squad’s Abloom damage.

The second addition in 2.8 is Starlight - Billy, also an S-Rank Agent, though wielding Physical Rupture instead. This is the upgraded form of Billy, and he arrives on a combat motorcycle to bring his signature Starlight Knight to the fight. Through it, he can deliver big Physical burst damage.

The higher Billy’s health, the more Sheer damage he deals. In fact, all Physical damage he deals lands as Sheer damage. Further building on his tank-like role, his skills can also restore his own health.

Re-runs in Version 2.8 will be Lucia in the first half, and Orphie & Magus in the second. The other exciting addition coming with this update is the new Wind attribute enemy, and the accompanying Vortex mechanic.

When an enemy is inflicted with the Wind Attribute Anomaly, any other Anomaly attack type that gets applied will trigger Vortex, rather than Disorder. This deals AoE Anomaly damage of the type that matches the corresponding element.

Throughout the version’s runtime, you’ll be able to take part in the Marcel Bootopia-themed event, which gives you control of Eous and lets you explore a Bangboo resort island. The island has been closed due to an outbreak of Hollows, and you must rescue Bangboos and find treasures.

If you do, you’ll earn Booltergeist and its Bangboo core for your troubles. This is an A-Rank Bangboo that can float around and fire lasers in combat. Its damage is further boosted whenever certain teammates are present.

The Ultimate Verdict Trial is another event you can check out that lets you fight alongside newcomer Promeia, or take part in other mini-activities that all reward Polychrome. Finally, you can look forward to a new Hoshimi Miyabi outfit: Dignified Blossom, which will be available in the store.

Before you jump back in next month, it always helps to catch up on the latest Zenless Zone Zero codes to make sure you’re not missing out on any freebies.

#4128. Genshin Impact Luna 7 brings us the first playable Hexenzirkel as things take a turn in Sumeru

Genshin Impact's Luna 7 update will kick off a new Archon Quest chapter, and deliver some interesting new additions to the playable roster.

HoYoverse just wrapped up a new Genshin Impact Special Program, where the developer revealed everything there is to know about the game’s next major update. Truth Amongst the Pages of Purana, or as its friends call it, Luna 7, was unveiled as part of the showcase.

This next update has a lot going for it, and it will be in players’ hands everywhere on May 20.

Luna 7 will take us back to Sumeru for its new Archon Quest, where a new crisis that threatens to plunge the nation into chaos is brewing. Nahida is out of the picture, and someone who looks suspiciously like Il Dottore has emerged.

If you complete this chapter at launch, you’ll earn up to 560 Primogems, as well as Nicole's Ascension Materials. Nicole is the first of three playable characters arriving with this update. Something else you’ll unlock if you finish the chapter quickly is a new Weekly Boss that HoYo says has “unpredictable abilities.”

And if you haven’t played in a while, don’t worry, you can refer to the Guiding Notes feature to catch you up on what’s been going on in the world. This is part of a larger effort from the team to make story progression more seamless, and also includes improved quest autosave prompts.

Nicole Reeyn is highest-profile and most interesting, being the first playable member of the Hexenzirkel. The mage is a 5-Star Pyro Catalyst wielder intended as a support member of the team. She can boost the ATK of all party members, even those not currently on the field. She also generates a shield while doing so.

Her Elemental Burst allows her to summon an Arcane Projection that follows the active character, sending out Coordinated Attacks that match their Elemental Type. Outside of combat, Nicole can help you find treasures by calling upon a Seelie to guide you to them. Quite fitting, as you’ll be exploring in the inside of the Witch's Lodge in Nicole’s Meeting Point in Luna 7, so bring her along.

Lohen, the Vice Captain of the Knights of Favonius' Fifth Company, is the second new character. Also a 5-Star addition, he is instead a Cryo Polearm wielder designed for aggressive combat. His main use is dealing massive Cryo DMG, and he can do that by managing two resources unique to him: Joy, and Will to Win.

Through his Elemental Skill, he can enter the Masterstroke state, allowing him to build up (and consume) Joy to unleash enhanced skills. The more his teammates fight, the more Will to Win he biulds, which can later be used to boost his effectiveness further. For an even more powerful display of force, bring along a Hexerei character when he’s on your team.

Prune is the third and final addition. Prune is a 4-Star Anemo Catalyst wielder, and her kit is inspired by her Witch Hunter aspirations. Using a bell and a hammer, she can deal DMG of several elements at once, and trigger Swirl reactions.

Nicole, and Lohen will debut in Luna 7’s first half, while Prune will follow in the second. The first half will also see a Durin rerun, with Mavuika returning in the second half. You can look forward to a new limited-time event as part of Luna 7, with a focus on Klee's Little Hexenzirkel.

You’ll find a series of mini-games you can play alongside Prune, as well as Qiqi, Yaoyao, and Sayu. If you play, you could earn the Super Awesome Magic Key, an exclusive weapon skin. Miliastra Wonderland is doing its thing, too, with a new sports festival for you to take part in.

One new gameplay addition worth calling attention to is that Manekins can now perform actions in Teyvat. The Kamera, which you can use to capture moments with Manekins, is getting upgraded, too, with new editing tools and assets.

Before you pick the game back up, be sure to check out our recently-updated Genshin Impact codes page for some free stuff you may be missing.

#4127. "Every piece is unified": Dark Messiah of Might and Magic returns with co-op, an Adventure mode, a level generator and New Game+ in the 64-bit Community Edition

First announced back in March, Dark Messiah of Might and Magic: Community Edition is a fan-made mod (for Dark Messiah of Might and Magic, obvs) that spruces up Arkane's 2006 RPG, including upgrading it to a newer version of the Source engine. Details have been scarce since then, but an updated Steam page confirms what other additions the mod – which is being made with the blessing of both Valve and original publishers Ubisoft – is making.

For one, as the Community Edition is rebuilt from the ground up using the contemporary Source SDK, the change in engine allows for both native Linux and Windows 64-bit support. Quality of life features like controller support are also listed, as are achievements, but the shining feature is the addition of co-op multiplayer, which will use Steamworks for P2P connections and hosting. So too will a "renewed" mutliplayer component, based on the original game's PvP mode. The Community Edition also boasts that "Every piece is unified. What you see in Singleplayer is accessible in Multiplayer, and visa-versa!"

Popular Dark Messiah mods that have existed for years have also been folded into the Community Edition, such as a New Game+ mode, a new Adventure Mode structure offering bonus levels and challenges, the addition of sliding as a movement mechanic, new spells, new weapons, new transformations; I mean, it's a mod attempting to gather up twenty years of modding into one rebuilt package, so you can imagine there's a lot here.

The community label extends to ensuring the community itself can contribute as they wish, with modders outside of the team granted tools to create custom elements, maps, and quests, alongside full Steam Workshop integration. While it isn't directly mentioned in the Steam page, the mod's development team wiltOS Technologies previously expressed their intent to build an RTX mod; with that 2023 blog post also mentioning a co-op mode, which is now being added, an RTX addition might still be on the cards. Either way, the Community Edition's release is currently set for 2026, which doesn't give it a lot of time for final, ray-traced accoutrements, but we'll see.

#4125. Dragon's Dogma 2 Is Getting Anime Crossover Updates Now, So Start Praying for Berserk

Dragon's Dogma 2 players have had a damn good run over the last few months, and Capcom doesn't appear to be ceasing support for its open world RPG anytime soon.

Having released the excellent Dark Arisen expansion in October — and reviving the title's popularity in the process — the developer is starting to roll out surprise collaborations.

Available in the game right now, a Delicious in Dungeon (also known as Dungeon Meshi) crossover adds two new outfits based on the comedic (and deceptively dark) manga and anime property.

You've got until the 29th January 2027 to redeem said costumes, which are based on main characters Laios and Marcille. They look great, and they come with adventuring backpacks!

You can find the sets in your storage upon loading up your save.

The update itself weighs in at 7.8GB, and also features a whole bunch of minor bug fixes. The official patch notes are available on the Dragon's Dogma 2 website.

Of course, this sudden collaboration begs the question: what's next? It'd be a bit weird for Capcom to wheel out a single crossover and then never speak of Dragon's Dogma 2 again — and so the smart money's on there being additional updates in the future.

Needless to say, we need that Berserk collab. For those who may not know, the first Dragon's Dogma, all the way back on PS3, had awesome armour sets from the dark fantasy manga — but re-releases removed them.

It's no secret that Dragon's Dogma as a whole was greatly influenced by the late Kentaro Miura's work, and so reviving the crossover would be amazing to see.
